pr_title: fix(ngcc): support inline `exports.<name> = <decl>` style exports in UMD files
pr_body:
UMD files export values by assigning them to the `exports` variable.
When evaluating expressions ngcc was failing to cope with inline declarations
like `exports.MyComponent = <decl>`.

Fixes #38947

comments:
So the reason for this error is that ngcc does not currently support parsing UMD/CommonJS properties of the form `exports.Xxxx`. It doesn't know how to interpret the `exports` identifier.

This is a bug in ngcc. The question is what priority we should give to fixing it.
Our experience is that UMD formats in libraries are usually not required for most use cases. Do you have concrete situations where this format is required?

As you said, if you just let the CLI do the work of running ngcc everything passes. This is because the CLI knows that your project does not need the UMD format, and just gets ngcc to process one of the other formats instead (e.g. ES2015).

By default running `ngcc` with no options will attempt to process every format of every package in node_modules. There are various ways to avoid this, such as adding the `--first-only` property or specifying a list of properties to consider (excluding `main` which maps to UMD) - e.g `-p esm2015 esm5 module browser`. Finally one can exclude the `main` property from just this package by adding a suitably configured `ngcc.config.js` file.

review_comments: These indentation fixes are on the wrong commit 😇
Could you add an explicit return for the `undefined` value?
Consider adding a code example here.

Should [this `if` block][1] be updated to correctly check for an inline declaration?

In general, looking briefly through the code-base, there seem to be several places where we check whether `declaration.node` is `null`. Previously, the respective branches would only be triggered for one type of `Declaration` (either concrete or inline).

Now that both types of declarations have a non-null `node` property these checks are either redundant (if we don't care about the type, but only about the presence of `.node`) or incorrect (if we _do_ care about the declaration type). Even in the first case (where the checks are redundant), it seems wasteful to operate on inline declarations if operating on concrete ones was sufficient before (unless the overhead is minimal and there are other benefits, such as simplified implementation).

Did I miss something?

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3cff332a99fb3006aeba2d0bbdf014a76bc48639/packages/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/host/esm2015_host.ts#L285-L287
You are right. I think we can remove most of the `xxx.node === null` checks.
The `isConcreteDeclaration()` check should be redundant if the previous `if` block is fixed to correctly detect inline declarations.
I couldn't work out how to make it redundant. If I remove it then `superDeclaration.identity` is not valid. Can you give me some more guidance here?

Looking at it again, we probably don't want to exit early if it is an inline declaration any more.
In which case, we just need to update the comment above the first `if` block (and keep the code as is):

```diff
-// If no declaration was found or it's an inline declaration, return as is.
+// If no declaration was found, return.
```

Is this really needed (given that we have `handler.compileFull as any` above?
I would expect only one `as any` yo be needed. (FWIW, if I had to choose, I would prefer to get rid of the one next to `hander.compilerFull` and keep this one.)
I removed the `as any` from the earlier line as suggested..
I think it is worth asserting that `decl.kind` is correct.
I believe the union of these two is just `ts.Node`.

There are lots of `ts.Node` types that cannot be assigned to `ts.Declaration` nor `ts.Expression`:

```
ArrayBindingPattern
Bundle
CaseBlock
CaseClause
CatchClause
ComputedPropertyName
Decorator
DefaultClause
ExternalModuleReference
HeritageClause
InputFiles
JSDoc
JSDocTag
JsxClosingElement
LiteralLikeNode
NamedExports
NamedImports
ObjectBindingPattern
PrivateIdentifier
QualifiedName
Statement
SyntaxList
TemplateSpan
Token<...>
TypeNode
UnparsedSection
UnparsedSource
VariableDeclarationList
```

Despite this, I thought I would see if that made any difference by changing the `DeclarationNode` to `ts.Node`. Initial results indicate that this fails compilation due to a lack of overlap between a number of types.

It is feasible that we could tweak the types in these places to get it to work, but this would probably result in more churn to the code.

Shouldn't this be:

```suggestion

```

No I don't think so. Previously we couldn't handle inline exports, which is why there are all these bailouts.
But now they are fully supported, and if there is a declaration that is inline but also has an import (`imp`) then it should not be a `TypeValueReferenceKind.LOCAL`.
I'm confused now 😕 Can you give an example of a `typeExpression` that has both an import and an inline declaration.

I think this is a scenario: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/e4424863c2cebdf3786f82c336294195d7733c93/packages/compiler-cli/ngcc/test/integration/ngcc_spec.ts#L580-L606

Here the `typeToValue()` function is needed to ensure that the "type" `ChangeDetectorRef` is also considered a value so that we get the correct information about it as an export.

If the `@angular/core` library in this test was packaged via ng-packagr as UMD then all its exports would be "inline".
If we didn't make the change here then these exports would be skipped, I believe.
I'll take your word for it 😆
Why not continue skipping inline declarations?
It appeared to me that skipping these was no longer needed since inline declarations now have `node` that can be targeted.
But do we want to have inline declarations in `exportMap`? Even if it's harmless having them in there, I assume we don't need them so why not skip them?

Absolutely, that is the main point of this PR, no?
This code is referenced when trying to find the declaration of an import from a 3rd party library. If that library is in UMD format and has "inline" exports then skipping them would result in the import failing to be found.
OOC, what do `expDecl` and `varExp` stand for?

`expDecl` -> export declaration : e.g. `exports.<name> = ...` or `var <name> = ...`
`varExp` -> variable export: e.g. `exports.<name> = <name>` (used when the export was defined as a variable.
I know it's horrible but I couldn't come up with something better that was succinct enough to appear all over the tests as these do.

I find the names confusing, but I can't propose better ones.
Maybe add https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/38959#discussion_r499180679 as a comment above each to make their purpose more clear.
